answer: A farm of a hundred aliases must park fresh stake on every key and wait through the same tundra of idle epochs, because the bond unlocks only after six consecutive passing answers and burns on copied text. A gale of last-minute registrations does not help: each alias still needs unique wording checked against a public karst of already-accepted answers, and shared phrasing voids both entries. Cheap keys stop being cheap once every one must sit, wait, and risk unrecoverable capital.
